subproblem.title: Approximate tangent planes of two locally finite sets agree almost everywhere on their overlap
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, W ⊆ ℝ^P open, and A, B ⊆ ℝ^P Borel with Hⁿ(A ∩ K) < ∞ and Hⁿ(B ∩ K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ W (Hⁿ = μHE[n]). Then for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ ℝ^P: if x ∈ W, x ∈ A and x ∈ B, then for every linear subspace Q, HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n A x Q ↔ HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n B x Q.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (W A B : Set (Euclid P)), IsOpen W → MeasurableSet A → MeasurableSet B → (∀ K : Set (Euclid P), IsCompact K → K ⊆ W → μHE[n] (A ∩ K) ≠ ∞) → (∀ K : Set (Euclid P), IsCompact K → K ⊆ W → μHE[n] (B ∩ K) ≠ ∞) → ∀ᵐ x ∂(μHE[n] : Measure (Euclid P)), x ∈ W → x ∈ A → x ∈ B → ∀ Q : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P), HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n A x Q ↔ HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n B x Q
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof Steps 3–4 (the densities of Hⁿ⌞(M∖F) and Hⁿ⌞(F∖M) vanish at Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M ∩ F ∩ W, and at such x the approximate tangent plane transfers between M and F); Simon Ch. 3, Remark 1.5(2) and the proof of Theorem 1.6 "⇒" (chapter-03.txt lines 86–90 and 113–146), stated symmetrically for two sets.
1. (Vanishing densities.) A∖B and B∖A are Borel, and for compact K ⊆ W, Hⁿ((A∖B) ∩ K) ≤ Hⁿ(A ∩ K) < ∞ and Hⁿ((B∖A) ∩ K) ≤ Hⁿ(B ∩ K) < ∞. Applying the sibling `local_density_zero` (whose open set is called U; take U := W) to S = A∖B and to S = B∖A gives an Hⁿ-null set outside of which: if x ∈ W and x ∉ A∖B then Hⁿ((A∖B) ∩ closedBall(x, ρ))/ρⁿ → 0, and if x ∈ W and x ∉ B∖A then Hⁿ((B∖A) ∩ closedBall(x, ρ))/ρⁿ → 0.
2. (At a good point.) Let x lie outside this null set with x ∈ W, x ∈ A and x ∈ B. Then x ∉ A∖B (because x ∈ B) and x ∉ B∖A (because x ∈ A), so both density quotients tend to 0 as ρ ↓ 0.
3. (Finiteness near x.) Since W is open, choose ε > 0 with ball(x, ε) ⊆ W and put r₀ := ε/2 > 0. Then closedBall(x, r₀) ⊆ ball(x, ε) ⊆ W and closedBall(x, r₀) is compact (ℝ^P is proper), so Hⁿ(A ∩ closedBall(x, r₀)) < ∞ and Hⁿ(B ∩ closedBall(x, r₀)) < ∞ by hypothesis.
4. (Conclusion.) The sibling `tangent_iff_density_zero`, applied to A, B, x, r₀ with Steps 2–3, gives HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n A x Q ↔ HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n B x Q for every Q. This holds for every x outside an Hⁿ-null set, which is the statement. ∎
proof_key_steps: A∖B and B∖A are Borel and locally Hⁿ-finite in W, so their densities vanish Hⁿ-a.e. on W outside them (local_density_zero).
At x ∈ W ∩ A ∩ B outside the exceptional set both densities vanish, and a small closed ball around x lies in W, giving finite measure near x.
tangent_iff_density_zero then transfers every approximate tangent plane between A and B at x.

audit.reason: Both set differences satisfy the localized density theorem. At almost every overlap point, openness supplies a compact neighborhood with finite measures, providing every hypothesis of tangent_iff_density_zero. Dependencies are correctly directed and non-circular.
